newsitem.title: UK: Iceland slips after disappointing H1.
newsitem.headline: Iceland slips after disappointing H1.

text.p: Shares in Iceland Group Plc eased in early trading after the food retailer reported disappointing first half results and repeated a warning that it expected 1996 profits to be below last year's level, traders said.
The company posted an eleven percent fall in pre-tax profits to 29.8 million stg compared with market expectations of betweeen 30 and 30.5 million stg.
Iceland also said overall like-for-like sales in the second half to date were down 0.5 percent, compared with a 1.0 percent decline in the second quarter.
By 0714 GMT the shares were down 2p to 100-1/2p.

"The figures are down on expectations. Whilst current sales have recovered slightly they have invested a lot of money and I think it's disappointing that sales aren't a bit more buoyant and I think we'll see more downgrades today," said one analyst.

Despite the warning on full year profits, chairman and chief executive Malcolm Walker said the actions being taken to improve stores, products, systems and price positioning were all designed to restore real growth to sales and produce improved returns for shareholders in the longer term.
But analysts said that signs of a turnaround in the group's fortunes have yet to materialise.

"They're a pretty gloomy set of figures. There is nothing in these figures that is at all optimistic. We may hear more at the meeting but I think if they had more to say they would have put it in the initial statement," said another analyst.
